transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess they brought me in because of what’s been happening at work. At the warehouse I keep doing things that don’t make sense to other people, like freezing with my arms up near the forklift, copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals, or moving boxes into these little patterns even when everyone’s yelling at me to stop.
Do you find yourself doing these things, like freezing or making patterns, when you're not at work as well?

Mostly it’s at work, that’s where people notice it. Like by the forklift I just freeze with my arms up, or I start copying the beeps and hand signals. And with the boxes, I’ll move them into these little patterns even when people are yelling at me to stop. I don’t really know why I do it.
Do you feel upset or bothered by these things you're doing at work?

I don’t know. I guess I’m more bothered when people start yelling or staring at me. The things themselves don’t always feel wrong while I’m doing them… it’s more afterward when everyone’s upset and I realize I messed something up.
Do you ever find yourself repeating certain behaviors or movements when you're alone or not at work?

Sometimes, yeah. I’ll catch myself doing little repeated motions, but it’s mostly at the warehouse where it gets bad. Like I said, I freeze up by the forklift with my arms raised, or I copy the beeping and the hand signals, or I start putting boxes into these weird little patterns even when people are telling me to stop.
Did you have any problems with speaking, walking, or other developmental milestones when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having problems like that, and nobody in my family has really told me I was late talking or walking or anything.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get stuck on things sometimes, but I don’t really know if it’s like thoughts repeating over and over. I haven’t noticed that as much.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you're doing these repetitive things, like freezing or making patterns?

Yeah, I guess I do get upset, mostly because I can’t seem to stop once it starts. Like at the warehouse, I’ll freeze with my arms up near the forklift, or I’ll start copying the beeping sounds and hand signals. Sometimes I move boxes into these weird patterns, and even when people are yelling at me to stop, I just keep doing it. It makes me feel confused and kind of overwhelmed.
Do you have any routines or rituals that you feel you must follow at home?
I don’t think so. At home I don’t really have a set routine or ritual I feel like I have to do. I mean, I do normal stuff, but nothing that stands out like that.
Do you have any strong interests that you feel are unusual or that others have commented on as being unusual?
Not really, no. I mean, I like certain things like anyone does, but I don’t think I have some unusual interest people point out or anything. Nothing comes to mind.
Do you have any strong preferences for how things are arranged or organized at home?
Not really. I don’t think I care that much how things are set up at home. If something’s messy I might notice it, but I don’t feel like it has to be arranged a certain way.
Did you exhibit any repetitive or restrictive behaviors as a child, such as hand flapping or insisting on sameness?

I’m not really sure. I don’t remember doing anything like hand flapping, and I don’t think my family ever told me I was really strict about things staying the same. Nothing like that stands out to me from when I was a kid.
Did you have any behaviors as a child that you repeated over and over, like rocking or spinning?
I don’t think so. I don’t remember rocking or spinning over and over like that as a kid, and nobody in my family has mentioned anything like that to me.
Did you have any behaviors as a child that were considered unusual or repetitive by your family or friends?
Not that I know of. I don’t really remember my family or friends saying I did anything unusual like that, or something I kept repeating. Nothing comes to mind.
Did you have any favorite toys or activities as a child that you played with repeatedly?
I’m not really sure. I had normal toys and games I liked, but I don’t remember playing with one thing over and over in a way that seemed unusual. Nothing really stands out.
Do you have difficulty making friends or understanding social cues?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I can talk to people when I need to, but I don’t always know if I’m reading things right. I wouldn’t say I’ve always had a lot of friends, but I don’t know if that’s because of social cues or just how I am.
Did you have any strong, highly focused interests as a child that you spent a lot of time thinking about or doing?
I don’t really think so. I had things I liked, but I don’t remember being locked into one interest or spending all my time on one thing as a kid. Nothing like that really comes to mind.
Did you have any intense or highly focused interests as an adult that you've spent a lot of time thinking about or doing?

Not really, no. I’ve had things I was interested in, like anyone, but I can’t think of one thing I got intensely focused on or spent most of my time thinking about. Nothing like that stands out to me.
Did your parents or teachers ever mention that you had a strong need for routines or rituals when you were growing up?
I don’t think so. I don’t remember my parents or teachers saying I had to have things a certain way or follow routines like that. Nothing really stands out to me from when I was growing up.
Did you ever feel like you had to follow certain rules or patterns in your daily life as a child?
No, I don’t really remember that. As a kid I don’t think I had rules or patterns I had to follow every day. I just kind of did normal stuff, as far as I can remember.
Did you have any unusual or highly restricted interests as a child that you felt very strongly about?
No, I don’t think I did. I had stuff I liked as a kid, but nothing unusual or like I was really stuck on it or couldn’t let it go. I can’t think of anything like that.
